title: Offline first desktop data in a JSON or embedded SQL file
when: The desktop app keeps all its records on the local disk and must choose between a JSON file and an embedded SQL file database, then store data safely.
prompt:
Goal: store.js keeps app data in the user data folder, loads fast, saves safely and makes daily backups, with the storage choice justified.
Steps:
1. Choose: under about 20,000 records and simple filters, one data.json loaded into memory is enough; heavy queries or large data need an embedded SQL file database.
2. JSON shape: { "schema": 1, "savedAt": "...", "items": [{ "id", "createdAt", "updatedAt", ... }] }; ids from crypto.randomUUID().
3. Load once at start, keep a Map by id in memory, save on change with a 500 ms debounce through the .tmp then move pattern.
4. Embedded SQL: Neutralinojs has no built in database; run it in a Neutralinojs extension process or load a WebAssembly SQL build from local resources, and always use bound parameters, never string built SQL.
5. Backups: once a day copy data.json to backups/data-YYYY-MM-DD.json and keep the last 7.
6. Export and Import menu items for a user readable JSON file.
7. Migrations run by the schema number before the UI renders.
Quality bar:
- The app opens and works with no network at all.
- A crash loses at most the last half second of edits.
Pitfalls:
- Saving the whole file on every key press without debounce.
- Concatenating user text into SQL.
Verify:
- [ ] Data lives under os.getPath("data").
- [ ] Saves are atomic and debounced.
- [ ] SQL, if used, has parameters only.
Output: store.js, migrations.js and a README data section.

examples.input: meu app desktop de estoque precisa funcionar sem internet
examples.output: data.json in the user data folder, in memory Map, debounced atomic saves, 7 daily backups
